# Business Associate & Vendor Risk Standard

**Organization:** Example Org
**Standard Owner:** Third-Party Risk
**Cadence:** Annual
**Governing Evidence:** Executed business associate agreements; Vendor security review records

## 1. Purpose and Scope

This standard establishes the requirements under which Example Org approves, manages, monitors, and terminates the exchange of information with other systems and with third parties, including business associates, external system service providers, and supply chain entities. It applies to all Example Org systems and to all internal and external parties that create, receive, maintain, or transmit information on Example Org's behalf.

Third-Party Risk owns this process end to end, including approval of exchange agreements, vendor security reviews, ongoing monitoring, and termination decisions and their handoffs to other teams.

## 2. Information Exchange Agreements

### 2.1 Agreement Types and Approval

Third-Party Risk must approve and manage the exchange of information between the system and other systems using interconnection security agreements, information exchange security agreements, memoranda of understanding or agreement, service level agreements, user agreements, non-disclosure agreements, or other organization-defined types of exchange agreement. [NIST 800-53 CA-3 | ARC-AMPE CA-3]

The appropriate information exchange agreements must be approved and in place prior to any information sharing. [ARC-AMPE CA-3]

### 2.2 Required Agreement Content

As part of each exchange agreement, Third-Party Risk must document the interface characteristics, security and privacy requirements, controls, and responsibilities for each system, and the impact level of the information communicated. [NIST 800-53 CA-3 | ARC-AMPE CA-3]

Third-Party Risk must enter into memoranda of understanding, memoranda of agreement, letters of intent, computer matching agreements, information exchange agreements, or similar agreements with parties (internal and external) that specifically describe the Personally Identifiable Information (PII) covered and enumerate the purposes for which the PII may be used. [ARC-AMPE CA-3]

### 2.3 Review and Update

Third-Party Risk must review and update information exchange agreements annually. [NIST 800-53 CA-3 — organization-defined frequency: annual | ARC-AMPE CA-3]

At a minimum, information exchange agreements must be reviewed and updated at least every one (1) year, and also following significant changes to the system, organizations, or the nature of the electronic sharing of information that could impact the validity or security posture of the agreement. [ARC-AMPE CA-3]

### 2.4 PII Sharing and Compatible Use

PII must be shared only in ways compatible with the purpose for which it was collected. Any subsequent sharing that is not compatible with the original purpose may not occur until additional notice is provided to the individual, their consent is obtained, and relevant documents are updated or published. [ARC-AMPE CA-3]

### 2.5 Termination and Suspension of Interconnections

The Authorizing Official or other senior leadership is authorized to order the immediate termination and/or suspension of any interconnection that, in their judgment and informed by senior cybersecurity or privacy officials, presents an unacceptable level of risk to the organization. [ARC-AMPE CA-3]

### 2.6 Data Transfer Authorization Verification

Example Org must verify that individuals or systems transferring data between interconnecting systems have the requisite authorizations (i.e., write permissions or privileges) prior to accepting such data. [NIST 800-53 CA-3(6) High]

### 2.7 Transitive (Downstream) Information Exchanges

Third-Party Risk must identify transitive (downstream) information exchanges with other systems through the systems identified in the information exchange inventory maintained under Section 2. [NIST 800-53 CA-3(7)]

Third-Party Risk must take measures to ensure that transitive (downstream) information exchanges cease when the controls on identified transitive (downstream) systems cannot be verified or validated. [NIST 800-53 CA-3(7)]

## 3. Access to Electronic Protected Health Information

### 3.1 Access Authorization Policies and Procedures

Example Org must implement policies and procedures for authorizing access to electronic protected health information that are consistent with the applicable requirements of subpart E of 45 CFR Parts 160–164. [HIPAA Security Rule 164.308(a)(4)(i)]

Example Org must implement policies and procedures for granting (and, based on access authorization policies, establishing, documenting, reviewing, and modifying) a user's right of access to electronic protected health information — for example, through access to a workstation, transaction, program, process, or other mechanism. [HIPAA Security Rule 164.308(a)(4)(ii)(B) Addressable | HIPAA Security Rule 164.308(a)(4)(ii)(C) Addressable]

### 3.2 Health Care Clearinghouse Separation

If a health care clearinghouse is part of a larger organization, Example Org must implement policies and procedures that protect the electronic protected health information of the clearinghouse from unauthorized access by the larger organization. [HIPAA Security Rule 164.308(a)(4)(ii)(A) Required]

## 4. Business Associate Agreements

### 4.1 Satisfactory Assurances

Example Org must permit a business associate (or a business associate's subcontractor) to create, receive, maintain, or transmit electronic protected health information on the entity's behalf only if satisfactory assurances are obtained, in accordance with § 164.314(a), that the business associate (or subcontractor) will appropriately safeguard the information. [HIPAA Security Rule 164.308(b)(1]

Third-Party Risk must document the satisfactory assurances provided by a business associate through a written contract or other arrangement that meets the applicable requirements of § 164.314(a); alternatively, an "other arrangement" satisfies this requirement if it meets the requirements of § 164.504(e)(3). Executed business associate agreements are retained as the evidence of record for this requirement. [HIPAA Security Rule 164.308(b)(3) Required | HIPAA Security Rule 164.314(a)(2)(ii)]

### 4.2 Required Business Associate Contract Terms

Business associate contracts must provide that the business associate will:

1. Comply with the applicable requirements of the Security Rule subpart;
1. Ensure that any subcontractors that create, receive, maintain, or transmit electronic protected health information on its behalf agree to comply by entering into a compliant contract or other arrangement; and
1. Report to the covered entity any security incident of which it becomes aware, including breaches of unsecured protected health information as required by § 164.410. [HIPAA Security Rule 164.314(a)(2)(i) Required]

### 4.3 Subcontractor Flow-Down

Example Org must apply the same business associate contract requirements to contracts or other arrangements between a business associate and its subcontractors as apply to contracts between a covered entity and a business associate. [HIPAA Security Rule 164.314(a)(2)(iii) Required]

### 4.4 Group Health Plan Plan Documents

Except where limited disclosures apply under § 164.504(f)(1)(ii)/(iii) or § 164.508, Example Org must ensure that a group health plan's plan documents are amended to require the plan sponsor to:

1. Implement administrative, physical, and technical safeguards that reasonably and appropriately protect the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of the electronic protected health information it handles on the plan's behalf;
1. Ensure the adequate separation required by § 164.504(f)(2)(iii) is supported by reasonable and appropriate security measures;
1. Ensure any agent to whom it provides this information agrees to implement reasonable and appropriate security measures; and
1. Report any security incident of which it becomes aware to the group health plan. [HIPAA Security Rule 164.314(b)(1) | HIPAA Security Rule 164.314(b)(2) Required]

## 5. External System Services

### 5.1 Provider Compliance Requirements

Example Org must require that providers of external system services comply with organizational security and privacy requirements and employ the [Assignment: organization-defined controls]. [NIST 800-53 SA-9 | FedRAMP SA-9 | ARC-AMPE SA-9]

Third-Party Risk must define and document organizational oversight and user roles and responsibilities with regard to external system services, and must include security and privacy roles and responsibilities in the service contract or agreement. [NIST 800-53 SA-9 | FedRAMP SA-9 | ARC-AMPE SA-9]

### 5.2 Ongoing Monitoring of Providers

Third-Party Risk must employ [Assignment: organization-defined] processes, methods, and techniques to monitor control compliance by external service providers on an ongoing basis. Vendor security review records are produced and retained as the evidence of this monitoring. [NIST 800-53 SA-9 | FedRAMP SA-9 | ARC-AMPE SA-9]

Third-Party Risk must include language in service contracts or agreements requiring the provider to be subject to U.S. Federal laws and regulations protecting PII and to adhere to the organization's security and privacy policies and standards consistent with 45 CFR § 155.260(b), and must consult legal counsel, the senior privacy officer, and contracting officers about applicable laws, directives, policies, or regulations that may impact implementation. [ARC-AMPE SA-9]

### 5.3 Risk Assessment and Approval for Security Service Outsourcing

Example Org must conduct an organizational assessment of risk prior to the acquisition or outsourcing of information security services. [NIST 800-53 SA-9(1) | ARC-AMPE SA-9(1) AE Mandatory]

Example Org must verify that the acquisition or outsourcing of dedicated information security services is approved by [Assignment: organization-defined personnel or roles]. [NIST 800-53 SA-9(1) | ARC-AMPE SA-9(1) AE Mandatory]

### 5.4 Provider Service Identification

Example Org must require providers of external system services to identify the functions, ports, protocols, and other services required for the use of such services: [Assignment: organization-defined external system services]; for FedRAMP, this applies to all external systems where federal customer data is processed or stored. [NIST 800-53 SA-9(2) Moderate, High | FedRAMP SA-9 | ARC-AMPE SA-9(2) AE Mandatory]

### 5.5 Trust Relationships with Providers

Third-Party Risk must establish, document, and maintain trust relationships with external service providers based on [Assignment: organization-defined security and privacy requirements, properties, factors, or conditions defining acceptable trust relationships]. [NIST 800-53 SA-9(3)]

Third-Party Risk must take [Assignment: organization-defined actions] to verify that the interests of [Assignment: organization-defined external service providers] are consistent with and reflect organizational interests. [NIST 800-53 SA-9(4)]

### 5.6 Location Restrictions for External Services

Example Org must restrict the location of [Selection (one or more): information processing; information or data; system services] to [Assignment: organization-defined locations] based on [Assignment: organization-defined requirements]. [NIST 800-53 SA-9(5) | FedRAMP SA-9 | ARC-AMPE SA-9(5) AE Mandatory]

For FedRAMP Certification Classes C and D, Example Org must restrict the location of information processing, information or data, and system services as defined; for Certification Class D, all federal customer data must be restricted to U.S./U.S. Territories or geographic locations where there is U.S. jurisdiction. [FedRAMP SA-9(5)]

In no case may the safeguards afforded to sensitive information be less than those mandated by state regulation, federal law, Executive Order, or other authoritative direction. [ARC-AMPE SA-9(5) AE Mandatory]

Example Org must process and store the system's PII within the continental U.S., Hawaii, or U.S. Territories. Support, development, and IT services may be off-shored, but the organization must weigh that risk, and Administering Entities must notify CMS at least sixty (60) days prior to committing to outsourcing information system services outside the U.S. (e.g., by contract award or services purchase). [ARC-AMPE SA-9(5) AE Mandatory]

### 5.7 Cryptographic Key Control and Data Integrity

Example Org must maintain exclusive control of cryptographic keys for encrypted material stored or transmitted through an external system. [NIST 800-53 SA-9(6)]

Example Org must provide the capability to check the integrity of information while it resides in the external system. [NIST 800-53 SA-9(7)]

### 5.8 Geographic Jurisdiction of Processing and Storage

Example Org must restrict the geographic location of information processing and data storage to facilities located within the legal jurisdictional boundary of the United States. [NIST 800-53 SA-9(8) | ARC-AMPE SA-9(8) AE Mandatory]

For organizations processing Federal Tax Information (FTI), Example Org must adhere to IRS Publication 1075 and must notify CMS at least sixty (60) days prior to transmitting data into an external information service environment per the Change Notification guidance. [ARC-AMPE SA-9(8) AE Mandatory]

## 6. Supply Chain Risk Management Policy

### 6.1 Policy Development and Dissemination

Third-Party Risk must develop, document, and disseminate to [Assignment: organization-defined personnel or roles] a supply chain risk management policy — at the [Selection (one or more): organization-level; mission/business process-level; system-level] — that addresses purpose, scope, roles, responsibilities, management commitment, coordination among organizational entities, and compliance, and is consistent with applicable laws, executive orders, directives, regulations, policies, standards, and guidelines, along with procedures to facilitate implementation of the policy and associated supply chain risk management controls. [NIST 800-53 SR-1 | ARC-AMPE SR-1]

Third-Party Risk must designate an [Assignment: organization-defined official] to manage the development, documentation, and dissemination of the supply chain risk management policy and procedures, with those officials named in the appropriate security and privacy documents. [NIST 800-53 SR-1 | ARC-AMPE SR-1]

### 6.2 Policy Review and Update

Third-Party Risk must review and update the supply chain risk management policy annually and following [Assignment: organization-defined events]. [NIST 800-53 SR-1 — organization-defined frequency: annual | ARC-AMPE SR-1]

At a minimum, the supply chain risk management policy and procedures must be reviewed and updated at least every one (1) year and following organization-defined events (e.g., assessment or audit findings; security or privacy incidents; changes to applicable laws, Executive Orders, directives, regulations, policies, standards, and guidelines). [ARC-AMPE SR-1]

## 7. Supply Chain Risk Management Plan

### 7.1 Plan Content

Third-Party Risk must develop a plan for managing supply chain risks associated with the research and development, design, manufacturing, acquisition, delivery, integration, operations and maintenance, and disposal of [Assignment: organization-defined systems, system components, or system services], addressing management, implementation, and monitoring of SCRM controls, supply chain risk tolerance, acceptable risk mitigation strategies or controls, a process for consistently evaluating and monitoring supply chain risk, approaches for implementing and communicating the plan, description and justification of mitigation measures, and associated roles and responsibilities. [NIST 800-53 SR-2 | ARC-AMPE SR-2]

### 7.2 Plan Review and Protection

Third-Party Risk must review and update the supply chain risk management plan at least every one (1) year or as required, to address threat, organizational, or environmental changes. [NIST 800-53 SR-2 — organization-defined frequency: annual | ARC-AMPE SR-2]

Third-Party Risk must protect the supply chain risk management plan from unauthorized disclosure and modification. [NIST 800-53 SR-2 | ARC-AMPE SR-2]

### 7.3 Supply Chain Risk Management Team

Example Org must establish a supply chain risk management team consisting of [Assignment: organization-defined personnel, roles and responsibilities] to lead and support [Assignment: organization-defined] SCRM activities. For ARC-AMPE, the team should include personnel with diverse roles — risk executive, information technology, contracting, information security, privacy, mission or business, legal, supply chain and logistics, acquisition, business continuity, and other relevant functions — collectively knowledgeable in acquisition processes, legal practices, vulnerabilities, threats, attack vectors, and system technical aspects and dependencies, and organizations should refer to current NIST SCRM publications (e.g., NIST SP 800-161, NISTIR 8276). [NIST 800-53 SR-2(1) | ARC-AMPE SR-2(1) AE Mandatory]

## 8. Supplier Risk Assessment and Analysis

### 8.1 Supplier and Contractor Risk Reviews

Third-Party Risk must assess and review the supply chain-related risks associated with suppliers or contractors and the system, system component, or system service they provide annually, considering security and SCRM processes, foreign ownership, control or influence (FOCI), and the supplier's ability to assess subordinate second-tier and third-tier suppliers and contractors, via reviews conducted by the organization or an independent third party. Vendor security review records are produced and retained as the evidence of these reviews. [NIST 800-53 SR-6 — organization-defined frequency: annual]

### 8.2 Analysis and Testing of Supply Chain Elements

Example Org must employ [Selection (one or more): organizational analysis; independent third-party analysis; organizational testing; independent third-party testing] of [Assignment: organization-defined] supply chain elements, processes, and actors associated with the system, system component, or system service. [NIST 800-53 SR-6(1)]

## 9. Supply Chain Agreements and Notification

Third-Party Risk must establish supply chain agreements and procedures with entities involved in the supply chain for the system, system component, or system service for the \[Selection (one or more): notification of supply chain compromises; [Assignment: organization-defined results of assessments or audits]\]. [NIST 800-53 SR-8 | FedRAMP SR-8]

For FedRAMP, supply chain notification agreements and procedures must follow the FedRAMP Incident Evaluation and Communication rules. [FedRAMP SR-8]

## 10. Documentation and Record Retention

Example Org must maintain the policies and procedures implemented to comply with the HIPAA Security Rule, and any documented action, activity, or assessment, in written (which may be electronic) form, retained for 6 years from the date of creation or the date when last in effect (whichever is later), made available to those persons responsible for implementing the procedures, and reviewed periodically and updated as needed in response to environmental or operational changes affecting the security of electronic protected health information. [HIPAA Security Rule 164.316(b)(1) | HIPAA Security Rule 164.316(b)(2)(i) Required | HIPAA Security Rule 164.316(b)(2)(ii) Required | HIPAA Security Rule 164.316(b)(2)(iii) Required]

## 11. Evidence of Compliance

Third-Party Risk is accountable for producing and retaining the following artifacts as evidence that this standard is operating:

| Artifact                               | Produced By      | Retention                                                                    |
| -------------------------------------- | ---------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Executed business associate agreements | Third-Party Risk | Per Section 10 (6 years from creation or last in effect, whichever is later) |
| Vendor security review records         | Third-Party Risk | Per Section 10 (6 years from creation or last in effect, whichever is later) |

These artifacts must be maintained in written (which may be electronic) form and made available to the persons responsible for implementing the procedures in this standard.
